newsitem.title: USA: Carter aide says China on long road to elections.
newsitem.headline: Carter aide says China on long road to elections.

text.p: China has begun a slow process of developing the technical capacity required for holding elections, a senior aide to former U.S. President Jimmy Carter said on Tuesday.
Robert Pastor, an elections expert with the Atlanta-based Carter Centre, headed a seven-member team that visited China March 5-16 to observe village elections in Fujian and Hebei provinces.

The Carter Centre delegation, whose help China solicited last November, also discussed election issues and areas of future cooperation with Chinese officials and left a set of suggestions for improving the voting process.

China's village election law, which began to replace an outmoded commune system in the late 1980s, allows an estimated 900 million village dwellers to elect local committees which oversee various development projects.

"The general view in the West has been that this is a sham, that the Communist Party is really very much in charge and it's really a way to delude the West into thinking maybe democracy's taking hold," Pastor told reporters.
"Our conclusion is that this is a serious and positive and significant development in China."
The Carter Centre, devoted to promoting democratic reform and humanitarian projects around the world, has overseen elections in a dozen countries including Haiti and Nicaragua.

Former President Carter oversaw the normalisation of U.S. relations with China during his administration. He later sponsored projects to train disabled individuals in the country and built a prostheses factory there.
